newsitem.title: UK: Major says can't rule out joining EMU first wave.
newsitem.headline: Major says can't rule out joining EMU first wave.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said the possibility that Britain might be among the first wave of countries to join a single European currency could not be ruled out.
"No one can rule that out," he said on BBC radio. "We can decide to take it or we can decide not to take it but there is a huge amount to settle, to be decided."
Major renewed his warning that he would stand firm if the European Court of Justice ruled against Britain in a case in which Britain has challenged an EU directive on a 48-hour maximum working week.
He said the Advocate General's opinion, delivered months ago, suggested Britain might lose the case and risk having restrictions imposed upon it.
"If that is so, that is something I don't think we would be able to accept without seeking a change in European law."

The proposals had been put through as health and safety measures. "Now we believe that is the wrong treaty base. It should not have been brought forward on that basis. It would damage our competitiveness," he said.
"I think we have to say, if we lose this case, it is not acceptable," he said.
